# Feature: ItemDefinition persistence lifecycle & security

<!-- auto-generated by /implement on 2026-09-06 — do not edit manually unless correcting intent -->

Issue: #136 · Slug: `item-definition-persistence-security` · Parent: #132 · Depends on: #134, #135

## Intent
Map the `domains/items` ItemDefinition contract onto the existing `inventory_item_definitions` catalog persistence so Personal/World definitions get a secure create/update/archive/restore/fork lifecycle, Core/builtin stay read-only, and taxonomy/provenance/`iconKey`/`assetKey` roundtrip without a parallel table or service.

## Preconditions
- Item domain taxonomy (#134) and item rules kernel (#135) are on the branch base / main.
- `inventory_item_definitions` + RLS + immutability triggers from migration 015 exist.
- `src/infrastructure/inventory/item-catalog-service.ts` is the UI-facing catalog boundary.
- No live Supabase is required for the offline contract script (same pattern as `inventory-catalog-check.mjs`).

## Happy Path
- [ ] Personal create/update/archive/restore persist via existing catalog infrastructure; `owner_user_id` comes from auth session, never from draft/form.
- [ ] World create/update/archive/restore bind only to a world profile from trusted/edit-authorized context; draft cannot retarget world or owner.
- [ ] Taxonomy fields, provenance, `iconKey`, and `assetKey` roundtrip through payload versioning; legacy payloads without taxonomy still parse with safe defaults and unchanged mechanical values.
- [ ] Fork from Core/builtin/World/Personal copies values into a **new** Personal or World id, sets `basedOnDefinitionId` / origin, and never overwrites the source id.
- [ ] Core / builtin definitions remain read-only at runtime (no update/archive/delete path).
- [ ] Archived definitions leave Add/authoring lists but remain resolvable by id for owned instances (active + archived lookup).

## Edge Cases
- [ ] Cross-owner Personal mutation/read attack fails closed (domain policy + repository filters + RLS contract).
- [ ] Cross-world World mutation/read attack fails closed.
- [ ] Rename does not change id; archive/restore changes status only.
- [ ] Fork of an already-forked definition references the immediate source only (no recursive inheritance).
- [ ] Concurrent update/archive cannot mutate another owner's row (null update → hard error).
- [ ] Unknown taxonomy / invalid draft rejected before write (`parseItemDefinition` + metadata validate).
- [ ] Attempt to mutate `core:*` ids is rejected in the repository before any write.

## Regression
- [ ] Existing `inventory-catalog-check`, `item-domain-taxonomy-check`, and inventory-v2 domain checks stay green.
- [ ] Architecture boundary: domains stay free of React/Supabase; infrastructure stays free of React/app imports.
- [ ] No second item-definitions table or parallel catalog service introduced.

## Security Coverage
`AGENTS.md` Non-Negotiables applied to this ticket:

| Item | Coverage |
|------|----------|
| Owner-scoped data stays owner-scoped | Personal writes filter `owner_user_id = auth.uid()`; owner never accepted from draft. |
| World scope enforced server-side | World writes use trusted `worldProfileId` argument + RLS edit helper; draft cannot set `world_profile_id` / scope. |
| No client-controlled identity | `id`/`scope`/`owner_user_id`/`world_profile_id` assigned or filtered by repository; payload strips identity on write. |
| Input validation at trust boundary | `assertWritablePayload` + `validateItemDefinitionMetadata` fail-closed before INSERT/UPDATE. |
| Archive not hard-delete | Status transitions only; Core never archived via this API. |
| Cross-tenant fail-closed | Pure `canMutateDefinition` policy + repository `.eq` ownership filters; offline attack tests in check script. |
| No secrets in logs | Errors are generic German strings; no payload dumps. |

## Assumptions
- "Built-in" means Core catalog / `origin: builtin-standard|core-archetype` sources that are not rows in `inventory_item_definitions` — read-only, forkable.
- World **edit** authority for live Supabase remains RLS (`current_user_can_edit_world_profile`); offline tests assert the pure policy + repository filter contract.
- Payload version `ITEM_DEFINITION_PAYLOAD_VERSION = 2` marks the taxonomy/asset-key contract; missing version = legacy v1-compatible read.

## Implementation Notes
- Owner: existing `inventory_item_definitions` via `item-catalog.persistence` / `supabase-item-catalog.repository` / `item-catalog-service` — no parallel table.
- `domains/items`: `ITEM_DEFINITION_PAYLOAD_VERSION` (2), `buildForkedItemDefinitionDraft`.
- `inventory-v2/catalog.ts`: taxonomy parse fail-closed, `canMutateDefinition` / `canCreateDefinition`, normalize on read.
- Repository: Core read-only guard; Personal updates filter `owner_user_id`; World updates bind `world_profile_id`; `forkDefinition`; metadata validate before write.
- Gate: `scripts/item-definition-persistence-check.mjs` (wired in `test-gate.mjs`).
- Offline only for attack/roundtrip contracts (same pattern as #107); live Supabase RLS unchanged from migration 015.
